title: [stacks-project]
statement:
Let $g\colon T\to Y$ be a quasi-compact immersion. The constructed map
$g^{\mathrm{im}}\colon T\to\operatorname{SIm}(g)$ is a quasi-compact open
immersion, and its image is topologically and scheme-theoretically dense.

mathlib_match.how: One declaration per clause, with a one-line specialization for sheaf injectivity. Openness: AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion.instIsOpenImmersionToImageOfQuasiCompact, Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Immersion.lean:259. Quasi-compactness: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.instQuasiCompactToImage, Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/IdealSheaf/Subscheme.lean:727. Topological density: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.instIsDominantToImageOfQuasiCompact, the same file:720. Scheme-theoretic density: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.stalkFunctor_toImage_injective, the same file:760, specializes TopCat.Presheaf.app_injective_iff_stalkFunctor_map_injective, Mathlib/Topology/Sheaves/Stalks.lean:546, at the structure sheaf of g.image and the presheaf morphism g.toImage.c; its forward implication applied to fun x => g.stalkFunctor_toImage_injective x gives injectivity on every open. These are the stalks of O_{g.image} -> (g.toImage)_* O_T at all points of g.image, including boundary points, not just the local-ring maps at points of T. The first instance needs IsImmersion g and QuasiCompact g; the others need only QuasiCompact g. No reducedness, Noetherian or quasi-separated target hypothesis is used. Revalidated after return of head 73fa1f9c97 against the current statement of def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image: its kernel ideal is the largest quasi-coherent ideal contained in the sheaf kernel, exactly Scheme.Hom.ker (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/IdealSheaf/Basic.lean:692), and its image is Scheme.Hom.image (Subscheme.lean:662). For the quasi-compact g in this item, Hom.ker_apply (Basic.lean:702) identifies that ideal with the ordinary kernel on affine opens. The factor g.toImage is itself quasi-compact by Subscheme.lean:727, so the density convention ker(g.toImage)=0 agrees with the injectivity established above and with def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open. The revised definition therefore changes neither the constructed object nor any clause or hypothesis of this item. Revalidated again for the landing return naming def-nagata-scheme-image-factor: its current statement explicitly defines the target using the largest quasi-coherent kernel subideal and the factor as AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.toImage g. Basic.lean:104 defines ofIdeals as the supremum of the quasi-coherent subideals, :125 gives le_ofIdeals_iff, and :692 defines Hom.ker using that operation. Subscheme.lean:662 and :665 define precisely this image and its inclusion, :710 defines Hom.toImage, and :715 gives Hom.toImage_imageι with no extra hypotheses. Thus the changed cited definition names exactly the same map as every declaration above; in particular none of the clauses concerns an arbitrary map into a merely topological closure. The statement dependencies remain valid on the current DAG.
